inputs.revenue_basis: NET revenue (revenue less pass-through costs), FY2025 = EUR 14,547m. This is the Groupe's headline KPI and the basis of every guided ratio (organic growth, operating margin rate 18.2%). Gross revenue incl. pass-through was EUR 17,399m; pass-through grew 38% in FY2025 and carries no margin, so compounding it would distort every component path. All margin/percent paths below are percentages of NET revenue.
inputs.share_count_basis: Number of diluted shares 253,343,182 at 31 Dec 2025 (FY2025 AR line 12213; equals the basic count because free-share plans are settled from treasury stock, so there is no incremental dilutive instrument). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and the EUR ~150m/yr buyback is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat (charging dilution as well would double-count).
inputs.net_debt_note: Publicis-defined net financial debt at 31 Dec 2025: financial debt 3,479 + fair value of hedging derivatives 4 = 3,483, less cash 4,031 = NET CASH 548 (FY2025 AR 5.4.2, lines 11951-11960). Financial debt INCLUDES earn-out liabilities and NCI buy-out commitments (EUR 677m of such commitments at year end, EUR 340m due <1yr), so deferred acquisition consideration is already deducted here and is NOT added to the forward M&A charge. Lease liabilities (EUR 2,182m) are EXCLUDED from net debt because the lease cash cost is charged inside the flows (treatment B). December is the right anchor: Publicis's working capital swings ~EUR 1bn negative at June, so an H1 balance sheet would understate the structural position.
inputs.balance_sheet_staleness: The FY2025 annual report (31 Dec 2025 balance sheet) is the latest filing in the corpus. The H1 2026 report (published ~July 2026) and the Q3 2026 net-revenue release (~mid-October 2026) are NOT extracted; refresh net cash and the FY2026 outlook when they are.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments' EUR 89m (line 12343; FY2024 91, FY2023 85). No separate equity-award withholding-tax line exists: French free-share plans are delivered from treasury shares, so the cash cost of the plans is the treasury-share purchases recorded as buyback_cash. The Groupe's own 'share-based compensation, net of tax' in the equity bridge is EUR 84m.
inputs.buyback_note: EUR 147m net treasury-share purchases in FY2025 (1,610,899 shares in Q2 for EUR 150m), FY2024 148m, FY2023 189m - a repurchaser that funds the flat count; dividends paid EUR 903m (DPS 3.75 proposed for FY2025).
inputs.owner_fcf_note: last_fcf = reported FCF (OCF 2,943 - capex 250 = 2,693) - SBC 89 - interest income 123 = 2,481. This is the post-interest, pre-lease, WC-inclusive figure for auditability only; the engine is UNLEVERED and component-built, so neither interest received nor interest paid enters the projected flows, and the net cash pile is added once in the bridge. For context, the Groupe's own 'free cash flow before change in WCR' was EUR 2,032m (after lease payments 453 and net interest 26, before the +234 WC inflow) - the component build's FY2026 pre-M&A owner FCF of ~EUR 1.9bn ties to that figure after taking out SBC and the FX headwind.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:28Z regular close (Euronext Paris, Friday; no later regular-session bar at build time)
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-denominated flows, EUR-built rate: 10y Bund ~2.8% risk-free, 5.5% mature-market ERP, beta ~1.05 for a large-cap cyclical advertising group gives a ~8.6% cost of equity; after-tax cost of debt ~2.9% on fixed-rate Eurobonds/USD bonds (Baa1/BBB+); debt at ~12% of EV gives 7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: AI-disintermediation, US-cycle and client-concentration risk are charged in the bear scenario's flows and its 25% weight, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full IFRS 16 cash payment (principal 367 + interest 86 = EUR 453m in FY2025, FY2024 also 453) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (3.1% of net revenue, drifting to 2.8% as the office footprint keeps shrinking - lease liabilities fell from 2,460 to 2,182 in 2025). Lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: reported D&A (excl. acquired intangibles) 520 less ROU depreciation 320 (line 13277) = EUR 200m = 1.4% of net revenue, so the lease is charged exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial and ignored: non-controlling interests are NEGATIVE EUR 23m on the balance sheet and the NCI share of FY2025 profit was EUR 12m (0.7% of attributable net income). Commitments to buy out NCI (EUR 63m) are already inside financial debt.
inputs.m_and_a_treatment: Bolt-on M&A is charged as a capex-like outflow inside capex_pct_path because it is a structural, recurring cash cost of the Publicis growth model, not optional: FY2025 EUR 670m (incl. 47 earn-out cash), FY2024 915, FY2026 guided c. EUR 900m. The growth paths correspondingly include acquired growth (~1.5-2pp/yr near term on top of 4-5% organic), consistent with the Groupe's +6-7% constant-currency net revenue ambition. capex_pct_path = tangible/software capex 1.7% + M&A 6.0% in FY2026, with the M&A component fading as growth decelerates to ~1.5% of net revenue in the terminal year. A valuation that credits acquired growth but omits the ~EUR 0.7-0.9bn/yr that buys it would overstate value by roughly EUR 25-30/share.
inputs.working_capital_note: wc_capture 0%: Publicis is a media-buying agent with very large offsetting receivables/payables; WC change was +234 in FY2025, -161 in FY2024, and the Groupe guides FCF 'before change in WCR' precisely because it is not forecastable. Zero capture is the neutral assumption; it is NOT a prepaid/deferred-revenue model.
inputs.tax_note: cash_tax_rate 25.5% base on component EBIT (vs. 25.1% effective rate). FY2025 cash tax of EUR 536m was flattered by a one-off ~EUR 98m US benefit (One Big Beautiful Bill Act, AR line 11904); normalised cash tax ~634 on component EBIT ~2,515 = 25.2%. Pillar Two and the French surtax keep the rate from falling.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year explicit horizon (FY2026-FY2035), engine route via make build-dcf. ROUTING: Publicis is an operating company (fee/commission advertising, media and consulting services) organised as a holding of agency networks - a management structure, not a financial holdco or compounder-of-book - so SKILL.md row 2 applies (non-US operating company with material IFRS 16 leases and a small NCI), owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md sections (a1) EUR WACC, (b) one lease treatment, (c) NCI, (d) excluded income has its asset in the bridge (interest income stripped, net cash 548 added once), (f) risk charged once. First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. BASE: net revenue, so EBITDA margin pre-SBC is 22.4% of net revenue (3,168 + 89 SBC) / 14,547 - equivalently 18.7% of gross revenue. FY2026 growth of 3.0% is organic +4-5% guided (management: '+4% is rock solid') plus ~2pp from c. EUR 900m bolt-on M&A less a ~3.5pp FX translation headwind at the guided EUR/USD 1.20 (vs ~1.13 average in 2025), which is why guided FCF before WC rises only to c. EUR 2.1bn; constant-currency growth of 5-5.5% resumes in FY2027. Terminal cap 15x FCF in base (cyclical, structurally sub-GDP fee pool) binds against Gordon 18.6x; bear 12x, bull 17x. Street basis (SBC as non-cash) sits ~6% above house (about EUR 7/share - 0.6% of net revenue capitalised at the 15x cap); band_position is negative because the price is below even the house value, i.e. the market is not paying for SBC treatment at all - the valuation risk sits in the M&A charge and the AI-fee-deflation bear path, not in the SBC band. PRICE: Friday 2026-10-23 regular close; not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance: organic net revenue growth +4% to +5% (AR 5.7 Outlook, confirmed with Q1 2026 net revenue on 14 April 2026), i.e. the midpoint before M&A and FX. The equity 5yr CAGR (7.8%) is not used as the anchor because it is inflated by the depressed FY2020 base and distorted by FX translation (EUR -1,291m OCI hit in 2025) and a 64% payout; the gross-revenue CAGRs are inflated by zero-margin pass-through growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 2.7% diverges >30% from EPS 3yr CAGR 10.6% and net revenue 3yr CAGR 5.0%: book value is held down by the 2025 USD translation loss and by returning ~64% of net income (dividends 903 + buybacks 147 vs net income 1,653). Not a signal about operating growth.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 2,678 / FY2022 2,054 / FY2025 2,481. The 5-year owner-FCF CAGR is negative only because FY2020 was flattered by a COVID-year working-capital inflow (OCF 2,966 on net income 576); FY2022-25 at +6.5% is the better read. Owner-FCF CAGR (6.5%) is marginally below reported (6.7%) because SBC grew from 64 to 89 - not a material SBC-growth problem at 0.6% of net revenue.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +3.0% reported EUR: organic +4.5% (guidance midpoint) + ~2pp acquired (c. EUR 900m bolt-ons) - ~3.5pp FX at EUR/USD 1.20. FY2027-28 5.5%/5.0% = the Groupe's +6-7% constant-currency ambition haircut for the fading new-business tailwind; then decelerating to 2.5% as the agency fee pool grows below nominal GDP.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA 22.5% in FY2026 = guided operating margin 'slightly above 18.2%' + D&A 3.6% + SBC 0.6%; +10bp/yr to 23.0% by FY2031 (AI production efficiency and Re:Sources scale, half the 2019-25 pace), flat thereafter.
base.capex_rationale: 1.7% tangible/software capex + M&A 6.0% (FY2026 c. EUR 900m) fading to 1.5% of net revenue in the terminal year as acquired growth fades with the growth path.

scenario_narratives.base: Publicis delivers its seventh year of outperformance roughly as guided: organic growth +4-5% in FY2026 led by Connected Media (Epsilon-powered data/media, retail media, CTV, creators), with Publicis Sapient flat and Intelligent Creativity stable; FX at EUR/USD 1.20 takes ~3.5pp off reported EUR growth, so net revenue grows ~3% in 2026 and ~5-5.5% at constant currency in 2027-28 before fading toward 2.5% as the agency fee pool grows below nominal GDP. The operating margin edges from 18.2% toward ~18.7% over five years as AI production tooling and the Re:Sources shared-service platform add leverage at half the 2019-25 pace. The Groupe keeps buying ~EUR 0.7-0.9bn/yr of bolt-ons (data, influencer, commerce, AI) to sustain ~1.5-2pp of acquired growth, and that cash is charged in full. Net cash of EUR 548m and ~64% payout continue. Terminal value capped at 15x FCF (below the 18.6x Gordon implies) because advertising is cyclical and the market has never granted Publicis a 20x free-cash-flow exit.
scenario_narratives.bull: The data moat compounds: Epsilon's identity graph plus the Power-of-One structure let Publicis keep taking share while WPP restructures (Elevate28, 9,000+ job cuts) and Omnicom digests Interpublic, so new-business wins keep adding ~2-3pp to organic growth and net revenue compounds 6-7% at constant currency through FY2029 - the top of management's own ambition - before decelerating to 3%. Agentic AI (CoreAI, Bodhi, Slingshot) proves to be a margin lever rather than a fee deflator, taking the operating margin toward 20% (pre-SBC EBITDA 24.5%) by FY2032, Publicis Sapient re-accelerates with the IT-consulting cycle, and the lease footprint keeps shrinking to 2.5% of net revenue. Bolt-on M&A continues at the same cash pace. Terminal cap 17x FCF and 3.0% terminal growth reflect a business the market finally re-rates toward a data/technology multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Generative and agentic AI disintermediates the agency value chain faster than Publicis can monetise it: clients in-house creative production, self-serve platform tools (Google, Meta, Amazon) and AI-native shops compress production and media fees, and Omnicom-Interpublic uses its new scale on pricing. A US consumer/ad slowdown (57-60% of net revenue) and continued stagnation at Publicis Sapient tip net revenue into mild decline in FY2028-29 (cumulative ~-1% over four years) before stabilising at 1.5% growth. Operating margin compresses ~3pp (pre-SBC EBITDA 22% to 19%) as the fixed cost base and the sticky lease footprint (3.0-3.2% of a shrinking revenue base) cannot flex with revenue, while management keeps spending on acquisitions to pivot (fading from 5.3% to 1.6% of net revenue). The balance sheet remains sound - this is a fee-pool deflation case, not a solvency case - but the terminal exit is 12x FCF at 1.5% growth, the kind of multiple the market puts on an ex-growth agency holdco.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25% because AI disintermediation of agency fees is a live structural threat to the whole industry, not a tail event (the stock has repeatedly dropped ~9% in a day on AI headlines, and Publicis Sapient is already flat), and 57-60% US exposure makes a US ad-cycle downturn a plausible trigger. Bull down to 25% because it needs two independent things to hold at once - continued share gains from rivals' disarray AND AI acting as a margin lever rather than a fee deflator - and the market has never paid a data/technology multiple for an agency group. Base at 50%: management has hit or beaten its organic-growth guidance for six consecutive years and guided FY2026 explicitly.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Publicis as what it is: a cyclical, high-cash-conversion services business whose growth is partly bought. The house basis charges SBC (small), the full IFRS 16 lease cash cost, a normalised 25.5% cash tax, and - the judgment that matters most here - the recurring EUR 0.7-0.9bn/yr of bolt-on M&A that funds the acquired component of growth, while crediting that growth in the revenue path. Terminal exits are capped at multiples the market has actually paid for agency holdcos (12-17x FCF) rather than at Gordon values. Risk is carried in the bear path and its 25% weight, not stacked into WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI disintermediation of agency fees (in-housing, self-serve platform tools, AI-native competitors) compressing both growth and margin - the bear axis
US macro / advertising cycle: 57-60% of net revenue is US-sourced and budgets are discretionary with short notice periods
EUR/USD translation: every 5% USD move is ~3pp of reported EUR net revenue and a similar hit to EUR FCF; FY2026 guidance assumes 1.20

M&A execution and price: the model assumes ~3x net revenue paid for bolt-ons keeps buying ~1.5-2pp of growth; overpaying or integration failure (Epsilon-scale deals) would make the capex charge insufficient
Client concentration: top 100 clients = 58% of revenue; a few account losses can remove a year of organic growth
Publicis Sapient (14% of net revenue) stays flat or declines with the IT-consulting cycle
Omnicom-Interpublic scale leading to renewed pricing pressure in US media buying
Balance-sheet anchor is the 31 Dec 2025 report; H1 2026 and Q3 2026 releases are not yet in the corpus
